name: Marau Wawa
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct Solomons language; only wordlists (Fox 1919 'Social Organization in San Cristoval', Ray 1926); no descriptive source.

sources.citation: Tryon, Darrell T. & Brian D. Hackman. 1983. Solomon Islands languages: an internal classification (Pacific Linguistics C-72). Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Marau Wawa appears only in the index of language names, starred as 'extinct or untraceable', location Makira Harbour, San Cristobal; no data, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Lanyon-Orgill, Peter A. 1947. Three languages of the South-East Solomon Islands. Journal of the Polynesian Society 56(3): 283-289 (Marau Wawa section pp. 285-287).
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Reprints Fox's word list, adds three words and the numerals ika/abut/kabut from an unpublished Houston MS, quotes Fox's 'peculiar singsong intonation', and gives 'Notes on Marau Wawa Grammar' (no incl/excl distinction, no article, undeveloped numerals, no conjunctions, single verb form, heavy use of hand signs). States the language 'has now died out', last two old men dying 1928 and 1930.

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1926. A Comparative Study of the Melanesian Island Languages. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press (San Cristoval chapter).
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number 2234.7.25)
sources.note: Named by the earlier scan as containing Marau Wawa word material; would be second-hand from Fox and is very unlikely to add prosodic information, but not verified.

sources.citation: Fox, C. E. 1924. The Threshold of the Pacific: an account of the social organization, magic and religion of the people of San Cristoval in the Solomon Islands. London: Kegan Paul, Trench, Trubner; New York: Knopf. pp. 44-46 (extended form of Fox 1919, JRAI 49: 94-179, pp. 130-131).
sources.note: Nothing on word stress. The whole record is ~9 'transposed Bauro' words, 4 'strange' words and 6 pronouns from the last surviving speaker; the only prosodic remark is (p. 44) 'The language is quite unintelligible to the people of the neighbouring coast and has a peculiar singsong intonation.' Fox says he took down a tale in the language 'which, with further information, must be dealt with elsewhere' (never published as far as can be traced).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page mara1417 (Hammarström et al.), endangerment comment citing Fox 1919: 130-131 and Lanyon-Orgill 1947.
sources.note: Nothing; only notes the language was very different from and unintelligible with Bauro and is almost certainly extinct. Zero descriptive references listed.

sources.citation: Fox, C. E. 1919. Social Organization in San Cristoval, Solomon Islands. Journal of the Royal Anthropological Institute 49: 94-179, pp. 130-131.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Original printing of the Marau Wawa passage; almost certainly identical in substance to Fox 1924: 44-46 (Lanyon-Orgill calls the book the extended form), so low value, but it is the reference Glottolog cites.
sources.venue: Journal of the Royal Anthropological Institute

sources.citation: Fox, C. E. (unpublished field notes, c. 1915-1918): the 'tale in the language' of Marau wawa that Fox 1924: 45 says he took down and would 'deal with elsewhere'; possibly among the C. E. Fox papers (Melanesian Mission / Church of Melanesia archives, or Auckland / SOAS holdings).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only connected text ever recorded in Marau Wawa; if Fox marked accent or length anywhere it would be here. Never published as far as can be traced.

sources.citation: Houston, R. (unpublished MS, before 1947): Marau Wawa words, numerals and grammatical notes, lent to P. A. Lanyon-Orgill (cited Lanyon-Orgill 1947: 285-287).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only other first-hand material on the language; Lanyon-Orgill printed only a few items from it. Whereabouts unknown (Lanyon-Orgill papers?).
